title: Mastering Notification Badges
summary: This reel outlines essential UI/UX rules for designing notification badges, focusing on layout stability, signal clarity, and user behavior. It teaches how to manage unread counts, distinguish between status and action, and maintain a high signal-to-noise ratio.

transcript.text: That red dot is a system.
One unread shows a single dot. 200 shows 99+. The cap keeps the shape stable.
The badge pins to the top corner. One digit or three, the icon never moves under it.
Red means act now. Green means online. A counting badge and a status dot are not the same object.
A dot says something changed. A number says how much. Showing both is noise.
It clears the second you open the view. A badge that lingers after you've looked trains people to ignore every badge.
When the count climbs, it ticks up. It never resets to zero on screen. That flash reads as a bug.
Badge only what needs a decision. Badge everything and the color stops meaning anything.
More UI systems at designmotionhq.com. Link in bio. Save this for your next build.

on_screen_text: Uncapped - the pill grows without limit
Cap at 99+ - width is bounded, layout holds
The badge pins to the corner - the icon never moves
A count is not a status - different signals, different rules
Dot or number - never both on the same row
A badge that never clears trains people to ignore it
Counts only climb - a reset to zero reads as a broken badge
Badge everything and nothing stands out - signal needs silence
before_after: Demonstrates the difference between 'uncapped' badges that break layouts versus 'capped' badges that maintain stability, and 'reflowing' icons versus 'anchored' icons.
